'''Greg Bole Rule With An Iron Fist''' is a [[Dark]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Greg Bole]]
* '''Published:''' July 1997 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Dagobah]]
* '''Side:''' [[Dark]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Tatooine: Lars' Moisture Farm|Premiere-D-tatooinelarsmoisturefarm.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Rule With An Iron Fist
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PDag Rule With An Iron Fist Bole DS 1997.txt |Download]]

== Introduction ==

Rule With An Iron Fist is a deck I created when the only set out was the Premiere main set of cards. Many rule additions and card additions from expansion sets have changed the playing field a lot, but some of the strategies used to put this deck together still hold. It might also be neat for newer players to see what the decks were like back in the "good old days" when only the first set of cards existed.

This is a tournament level deck which costs a lot of money to put together, it's not the kind of deck most people would create to just play fun games with friends. But for those who want to compete at large sized tournaments (or just really crush their Light-side friends) you have to cut your deck down to use only the most effective, efficient, and powerful cards which closely fit your theme.

== Strategy ==

My first deck submission! This is a money deck, no two ways about it. It's very expensive and assumes you have all the rares and duplicates of the main characters, the most expensive cards in the game. But these are the kind of decks you will often see at high-powered tournaments. The main theme of this deck is to rule Tatooine with an iron fist on either the land or in space with the possibility for controlling additional systems.

'''Strategy:'''Deploy in force to a Tatooine site, establish an unbeatable presence and force drain each turn. If the sites become too hairy (for whatever reason) the whole operation can easily be taken aboard a Star Destroyer and/or Vader's TIE to drain for the same amount at a system. If the opponent dares to deploy 2-4 characters alone, transport your entire strike force with Elis Helrot and hit them for a huge battle loss.

'''Locations:'''The locations were chosen for a number of reasons: a) High force generation in order to deploy the mains and the ISDs b) Bonuses to force drain on Tatooine, the starting location allows a force drain of 2 a turn, which should be increased to 3-4 by lightsaber wielding characters. c) No Death Star sites at all so you don't have to worry about protecting two fronts. The often used DS: War Room was avoided for this reason and because of the text allowing the LS to get an extra battle destiny when attacking there.

'''Characters:''' The characters used can be divided into three main categories:

1. High Ability Imperials - the team of Lord Vader and Grand Moff Tarkin is almost unstoppable and four of these characters have high ability and can easily wield lightsabers for boosted force drains and to kill the opponents main characters.

2. Imperial Pilots - both unique TIE pilots give a 3 bonus to starships but can also be shuttled to sites to help defend or attack. The combination of all six Imperials in one battle with Jedi Presence is deadly.

3. Aliens - the infamous team of Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba would have won the Cantina skirmish if Darth Vader had been there to strike down Obi-Wan. Ponda gets a power bonus with the "good doctor" who in turn can be used to operate on hit opponents to remove them from the battle

'''Starships:'''The Star Destroyers can be used to force drain at systems, shuttle around characters, and add a +1 bonus per ship to battles on Tatooine when you control the system. The Scouts can act as attrition fodder to keep the ISDs flying and have greater range with their higher number hyperdrives.

'''Vehicles:'''The Sandcrawler, with it's ability to carry up to eight passengers, react capabilities, and power of two, is the ultimate vessel of doom for Tatooine strike forces.

'''Weapons and Devices:'''As mentioned before the lightsabers are an integral element of this (and almost any) deck. They provide the ability to drain greater amounts of force and kill your opponents main characters. The comlink is to deploy one character at a second or third force draining site with the ability to rescue him by reacting with even more forces from your hand.

'''Effects:''' Presence Of The Force should be deployed where ever your main force is draining to give you not only +1 to your force drain but also one more force to activate every turn. Just don't let that site fall into Rebel hands. Reactor Terminal is a must to recirculate high destiny cards back into your deck near the end of the game in order to have guaranteed high weapon and battle destiny draws. Another nasty tournament trick is to get almost your entire hand back into your life force the turn before you win to boost up your life force points for your win.

'''Used Interrupts:'''Until they are more balanced Senses and Alters are the name of the game. If you have more than your opponent your Interrupts and Effects work while theirs are canceled. If you win a large "Sense War" (where each of your keep cancelling the others one after another) whoever gets the last one out keeps them all, the loser loses them all...creating a major tactical advantage for the winner. As mentioned before the Elis' are there to transport your hit-squad onto Yavin 4 for a huge invasion or to wipe out a smaller force that's running from you on Tatooine.

'''Lost Interrupts:'''These high-powered rares speak for themselves. They either add large amounts of battle power and/or destiny draws or can be used to eliminate your biggest threat - the old Jedi Knight himself, Obi-Wan Kenobi.

'''Opening Strategy:''' If you get lucky enough to have one of your Vaders and Tarkins in your opening hand you are in really good shape to start your reign of terror early. If you don't then play any locations you get and wait at least until you have Vader and either Tarkin, or one of Vader's Interrupts and a lightsaber. Then you can start saving force to get the Dark Lord of the Sith out on Tatooine to begin his evil control of the planet. Once you start generating a decent amount of force (deploying each location as you draw it) you can save force to bring out your Imperial support troops and at the same time continue to draw cards into your hand to build your reinforcements.

'''Mid-Game:'''Your stratgegy here is pretty straight-forward. Rule with an Iron Fist. Keep control over one location draining your opponent for 2-4 force a turn (depending on how many lightsabers you draw and when the Presence of the Force comes out). If they are draining you elsewhere you might have to ready an attack. This can be done easily with Elis Helrot, or be mobilized and supported by a few Imperial Star Destroyers. If you have over 12 power (which shouldn't be hard with Lord Vader out) and an Interrupt like Jedi Presence of I Have You Now, then transport to where the Rebels have dared to deploy and crush them under your heal. However you must be careful of comlinks, CZ-3s, vehicles, and other things that allow your opponent to react to a battle. They could have a desperate, yet cunning, Rebel trick up their sleeves.

'''End-Game:'''After sustaining heavy losses due to your force drains and a major attack or two the Rebel scum will be weakened. If they lose a long Sense War you will have the upper hand to brush aside any Interrupts that might give them an edge. Either continue to slowly tighten your grip on the throat of Tatooine, crushing it's force between your fingers, or swoop in for a final blow that will finish them off. The only real threats to your overwhelming forces would be a) Obi-Wan with a lightsaber b) many extra destiny draws against you through the use of a combination of Interrupts or c) a suprise counterassult by their ability to react to a force drain or attack. Of course you have ways to counter each of these threats:

A. Darth Vader with a lightsaber is a good match for Obi-Wan, even better if you play The Circle is Now Complete, and of course if Tarkin is there with Vader one of Obi-Wan's *weapon* destinies can be cancelled instead of a battle destiny (a point many players don't realize)

B. Tarkin, with Vader, can cancel at least one of these battle destinies and your Sense superiority should be able to cancel any particularly nasty Rebel Interrupts. The only way one of your Senses could fail, if Vader is on the table, is if you draw the only card in your deck with a destiny of 6...The Circle is Now Complete. The reason this is included is it's great usefulness in eliminating Vader's only real threat, and the Light Side's only chance to assure Sense draws: Obi-Wan and his 6 ability.

C. You do have to be careful of Rebel reacts, but remember Sense cards can cancel reacts as well as Interrupts!

The strength of this deck is sheer power combined with the ability to shut down Rebel opposition. If you deny your opponent the chance to deploy, use main characters, play Interrupts, and react to your threat, then you have the upper hand and control play. Long Live The Empire!

This is not a deck for the weak of heart. It combines raw power and several devious Imperial tricks to "crush their insignificant rebellion".
